notes: Round 6 (2026-11-08): a kernel-checked counterexample family for the extension-field decomposition heuristics: subfield curves with odd extension degree confine every factor-base sum to E(F_q).

sources.title: SubfieldFactorBase: the x in F_q factor base of a subfield curve never leaves E(F_q) (Lean, 2026-11-08)
sources.citation: research/ecdlp_weakness_lean_20261104/lean/SubfieldFactorBase.lean (Lean v4.34.1 / Mathlib v4.34.1; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound).

nodes.label: Subfield curve, odd n: every sum of x in F_q factor-base points lies in E(F_q), at most 2q + 1 points (Lean)
nodes.statement: Let W be a Weierstrass curve over a field K and L/K an extension of odd degree. A root in L of a monic quadratic over K lies in K, so every point of W(L) whose x-coordinate lies in K is the image of a point of W(K); hence the subgroup generated by the factor base F = {P : x(P) in K} lies in the image of W(K), and over a finite K with q elements the decomposable points (sums of any number of factor-base points) number at most #W(K) <= 2q + 1.
nodes.scope: Curves defined over the subfield F_q and odd n only. For n >= 3 this contradicts any Omega(q^(n-1)/(n-1)!) or 1/n! decomposition count on this family, while #F >= #E(F_q) - 1 >= q - 2 sqrt(q) (Hasse, cited, not formalised). Says nothing about curves whose coefficients generate F_{q^n}.

nodes.label: 'Omega(q^(n-1)/(n-1)!) decomposable points whenever #F in Omega(q)', over all E/F_{q^n}
nodes.statement: Literal reading of Joux-Vitse Assumption 1 as recorded: for every elliptic curve E/F_{q^n} whose factor base F = {P : x(P) in F_q} has #F in Omega(q), the number of points that are sums of n - 1 factor-base points is Omega(q^(n-1)/(n-1)!).
nodes.scope: False for every curve defined over F_q with n >= 3 odd: the hypothesis holds (Hasse) but at most 2q + 1 points decompose. The assumption needs an extra condition excluding subfield curves (and, for even n, curves whose factor base sits in E(F_{q^2})).

nodes.label: msolve F4 on a fresh m = 2, n = 37 instance runs a degree-5 step
nodes.statement: msolve 0.6.5 (F4, grevlex, 4 threads) on a fresh pq2_rank instance at n = 37 (m = 2, factor-base dimension 19 = ceil(37/2), field equations included; 38 variables, 75 equations) ran steps of degree 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 4 and then a degree-5 step on a 1,016,044 x 610,665 matrix, about 60 minutes in at 53 GB, on an isolab-eks cpu-spot node. F4 selects the lowest-degree pairs first, so msolve's maximal step degree on this instance is at least 5.
nodes.scope: One instance; one implementation (msolve, not Magma); run unfinished at recording, so the final Groebner basis check (linear = k = 33) is pending. A lower bound valid for every F4 run would need the degree-4 closure to fall short of k (about 58 hours at this size).

edges.statement: Subfield curves with odd n >= 3 satisfy #F in Omega(q) (Hasse, cited) and have at most 2q + 1 decomposable points.
The recorded hypothesis #F in Omega(q) is not sufficient; the assumption can hold at most for curves not defined over a proper subfield containing the factor base.
On subfield curves with odd n the 'no unexpected collisions' assumption fails wholesale: every n-sum lands in E(F_q), so the proportion is at most about 2q/q^n, not 1/n!.
A factor base inside a proper subgroup confines all decompositions to that subgroup, whatever its size.
The census's subfield-curve control at n = 3 measured decomposable fractions 0.0003 to 0.002, against 1/6.
On the diagonal k = ceil(n/m) at m = 2, n = 37, msolve's F4 runs a degree-5 step: d_F4 > 4 for this implementation (Semaev's quantity is Magma's).
Reproduces with a second implementation the step from degree 4 to 5 that Kousidis-Wiemers report for Magma from n = 37.
